Could an agreement not to disclose things be done informally via email or verbally? Sure. But NDA's are notoriously difficult to litigate anyway. Many that are written by lawyers fall apart under the judge's withering stare. Informal NDA's are likely to be found entirely toothless.

The problems are several.

You have to prove that the NDA was reasonable in scope and duration. "YOU CAN'T REPEAT ANYTHING I SAY EVER TO ANYONE NA NA NA NA NA NA" is probably NOT reasonable in scope and duration and that's what these email signatures boil down to.

You have to prove that the data WAS confidential and valuable. Not everything you say is confidential or valuable.

You have to prove actual harm from disclosing it. If we're just talking about bid quotes... and they shopped your bid to get lower prices... the problem is you can't prove they ever intended to hire you. It was never YOUR money to lose.

You have to demonstrate consideration for a contract to be valid. What tangible benefit are you giving your customers in exchange for swallowing a gag order? Is what you give relatively appropriate in relationship to what you request? (The 'right' to see your quote is likely not a valuable commodity, compared to their general right to freely communicate and transact business, which is what you're asking them to limit on your behalf.)

NDA's are difficult to get enforced even when they're well written and signed by a party who's had a meeting of the minds and received consideration. When they're sprung on you after you've already read an email and you received nothing in return, they're downright laughable. If you have legitimate confidentiality concerns, talk to a local lawyer who specializes in business law and who can provide you examples of NDAs that have survived a challenge.

And then there's the issue that in many industries... if you start suing potential clients for not hiring you... you're going to find that nobody wants to get a quote from you any more... for some reason.

Activities with friends:
Transportation: 10€
Booze: 20€
Food: 20€

If the 2$ public transport + 10$ booze buys you one evening of fun with your friends and creates good memories then it's not a waste of money. It's an investment on your mental health. You are not alone; we all at times in some way hate ourselves. Self confidence is a deep seeded thing and believe it or not, the source of any of these problems lies in how you see truth. Until someone respects the absolutes of life, they can never respect themselves. There is, of course, false self confidence. It manifests itself as feeling good about you, having the courage to act on your own choices, and being untouched by the perceptions of others. However, any of those things do not necessarily equate to truly respecting yourself and others. They are simply a result that can come from many things. What you want to build in yourself, however, is real confidence - that which doesn't vary with situation or practice, but it only comes from real sacrifice. We are taught in every culture to follow a set of rules. These rules are seen as important and function to hold a society together. But the mistake that is made is seeing how reality is shifted by these rules and making the assumption that truth itself is a social construct. We don't do this intentionally in our minds. We may truly believe in absolutes mentally. However, in our hearts is where this mistake is made and it bleeds into our actions and our feelings because of it. We may tell ourselves we know something is true, but our hearts will always act out the truth that is inside us. So you can tell yourself you care about someone, but when the day comes to actually care, you may find your heart empty and unable to act. It is the same in this case. You may tell yourself that you love yourself and see yourself as valuable. You may mentally consent to the ideas that you are pretty or fun, but in your heart, it is empty. Furthermore, many people do not analyze themselves or their actions. They simply lay over their wounds psychology or some other construct to help calm the problem, rather than finding the root of it in their heart. It's easier to find a comfortable mental lie, than to get to the heart of a problem and deal with the actual issues. Anyway, if you want actual confidence live by what is actually true. You need to stop getting your value or creating your values by the perceptions of others. There is actual value and dignity to things. There are set real ways of going about treating things with respect that have nothing to do with a social creation. A truck will kill you if it hits you on the highway. People didn't determine that. Your feelings don't determine that. Your breasts are two little fun bags that feed babies and incite erotic pleasure. People didn't determine that. Your feelings don't determine that. A darker tone looks pleasant on a lighter canvas. Rich color creates contrasts that evoke all sorts of things. People didn't determine that. Your feelings don't determine that. You are not the center of truth. People are not the center of truth. Your feelings do not make something absolutely real, they just govern your actions which could be or could not be worthy of the time they take to do. The sacrifice then is to remain consistent. If you are going to stop putting confidence your ability or other's ability to create what is real and believe that there is truth outside of a social construct, that means living your life seeking the truth of all things and not just settling for some created version, aligning your life and your principles correctly. But as you actually live that way, you will get greater confidence in the truth, and, as a result, stop being governed by your feelings or what everyone else thinks, or, even what you think. That's where true confidence manifests itself -in a changed life willing to take the hit of not being accepted or agreed with or appreciated, and continuing to live life without fear of the result of being true, because truth matters more than its result. Your feelings are not your reality. Only you can choose not to hate yourself. Don't let what you feel be your reality anymore. There are greater things that determine truth than you or your friends.
